chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Suleyman ibn Salih, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'What is the lowest form of extravagance?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Your degrading your protective garment, and pouring out the remainder from your vessel, and eating the dates and discarding the pits here and there.'

key_terms.ثَوْبَ صَوْنِكَ: Your protective garment (clothing kept for wear)

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum level of extravagance according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) redefines the threshold of *israf* (extravagance/waste) by focusing on the neglect of utility rather than mere excess, highlighting that discarding wearable garments or leftover sustenance constitutes waste. This perspective aligns with Shia scholarly emphasis on *iqtisad* (moderation) and the spiritual danger of *kibr* (arrogance) that often accompanies the careless disposal of blessings. The examples of date pits and garments serve as practical indicators for daily mindfulness in resource management.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Salih Bin Uqba, from Suleyman Bin Salih who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What is the lowest of the extravagance?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Your routinely wearing of your protective clothing, and your discarding the remnants of your utensil, and your eating the dates and your throwing with the core over here and over there’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il from Salih ibn ‘Uqbah from Sulayman ibn Salih who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the least degree of squandering. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is misuse of protective clothes, throwing away the remaining water in your bowl and when eating dates throwing the date-stone here and there.’”
